What do if someone is completely adamant in their refusal to seek professional help?

It's tricky, but there's not much you can do except be supportive. It's a decision they have to come to on their own; if you try and force the issue you just make it more likely that they'll reject the idea. "You need help" is far less useful than "have you thought about getting help". If they refuse, it's ultimately their call and you would just work around it. The biggest part is them deciding to make whatever adjustments they need to in order to address the problem. Anything you can do is great and all, but won't 'fix' whatever issue they face, real or perceived.

At what point do you think some sort of intervention is needed? If the person is self-harming or is saying things that seem to indicate suicidal thoughts, isn't it better to err on the side of caution for a loved one?

And do what? Honestly it's not a bad feeling you're having and it makes perfect sense, but what would you do? It's a rare and extreme case that would allow you to place a person into treatment involuntarily; they often have to do something way off the scale for it to register for the state and self harm isn't even close unfortunately. At best keep and eye out for signs they've actually made the decision to follow through, which unfortunately can vary from person to person. If you're a a point of real worry, perhaps you should seek out the professional help yourself and see what they have to say about the situation. They will be able to give you far better advice than any of us can.
